significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) law that CoT faithfulness declines with a model's independently defined "language dominance/resource level" even at matched accuracy, together with the form-(ii) mechanism that engagement of a steerable "CoT-reliance" signal causally controls this gap. This would predict not only perturbation sensitivity across languages but also when monitor recall should deteriorate, directly constraining the use of CoT monitoring studied in Turpin et al. (2023), Lanham et al. (2023), and later reasoning-monitoring work. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a candidate mechanism; verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable, and an accuracy-controlled null would rule out language-specific decoupling, although failure of the reliance signal alone would only reject that mediator. In the topic-substitution check, the generic language–intelligence topic would not imply an accuracy-independent dominance–faithfulness law or its monitorability consequence, so the score is supported by claim-specific content rather than the topic's general importance.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two named handles: "language dominance, defined ex ante from training-data/resource proxies" as a forward-looking risk predictor and a steerable "CoT-reliance" direction as an intervention, rather than merely a post-hoc explanation. The dominance handle has lead time because it can flag languages before rationale-based monitoring is trusted or deployed, while the reliance direction can be used to "restore or remove CoT-reliance"; downstream users therefore include model auditors and deployers, not only multilingual-interpretability researchers. After model-specific re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a transferable relation—lower dominance predicts lower faithfulness and lower reliance predicts reduced perturbation sensitivity—across the asserted class of multilingual LLMs and math, logic, and multi-hop tasks, even though the particular activation direction may require recalibration. The topic-substitution check does not preserve these handles or their ex-ante action window: merely investigating language and intelligence would provide neither a dominance-based monitoring rule nor a predicted cross-model relation.
